papers.title: A rare TMEM175 mutation drives Parkinson's disease pathology by disrupting proton gating and lysosomal acidification.
papers.abstract: Transmembrane protein 175 (TMEM175), implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD) risk, has been variably proposed to function as a background K+ "leak" channel or a proton-activated proton channel in lysosomes. Here, we identified the rare TMEM175 variant p.L275R in a patient with early onset PD. Electrophysiological analyses revealed that TMEM175-L275R mutant proteins retain normal lysosomal expression and K+ "leak" activity, but specifically lose proton- and agonist-dependent activation gating. In skin fibroblasts isolated from the patient with PD harboring the monoallelic p.L275R mutation (TMEM175+/L275R), and in derived induced pluripotent stem cells and induced dopaminergic neurons, lysosomal H+ flux, acidification, and degradation were impaired. These lysosomal defects were corrected upon genome editing to produce the isogenic WT allele (+/+Cor), but appeared when the mutant allele was introduced onto a WT background (+/L275RMut). Pathological α-synuclein aggregation was facilitated in patient-derived (+/L275R) and mutation-introduced (+/L275RMut) neurons. Consistent with these genetic findings, pharmacological activation of TMEM175 with small-molecule agonists restored lysosomal functions and reduced α-synuclein aggregation in TMEM175+/L275R neurons. In in-vivo studies, equivalent-site-mutation knock-in mice demonstrated synucleinopathy and PD-like motor phenotypes. Collectively, our work provides genetic and pharmacological evidence that severe loss-of-function mutations may contribute causally to the onset age and pathogenesis of PD and identifies lysosomal proton channels and transporters as potential therapeutic targets for PD intervention.

papers.title: Ultrasound-Guided Mobilization of Dual Autophagic Cleaning Crew by Exosomal Rapamycin Ameliorates the Progression of Parkinsonism.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Autophagy dysfunction is a key contributor to Parkinson's disease (PD) pathogenesis, driving α-synuclein (α-syn) accumulation and progressive dopaminergic neurodegeneration. Although enhancing autophagic clearance of α-syn represents a promising therapeutic strategy, achieving controlled modulation of autophagic flux while maintaining neuronal viability remains challenging. METHODS: A focused ultrasound (FUS)-enabled exosomal rapamycin delivery platform (EXO-RPM) was designed to modulate autophagic degradation in PD models. We systematically characterized their morphology, physicochemical properties, and environmental stability. In vitro studies assessed cellular uptake, cytotoxicity, autophagy induction, autophagic pathway modulation, and α-syn clearance. Subsequently, ultrasound-guided brain accumulation, behavioral recovery, brain immunofluorescence, and positron emission tomography (PET) imaging were evaluated in vivo. Finally, the biosafety of the nanoplatform was evaluated via histopathological and biochemical analyses. RESULTS: Under optimized conditions, EXO-RPM achieved a high encapsulation efficiency of 90.14%. This platform exploits endogenous transferrin-transferrin receptor interactions for brain-targeted delivery, while FUS provides spatiotemporal control by transiently opening the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and thereby enhancing drug accumulation in the brain parenchyma. Following FUS-mediated delivery, EXO-RPM reduced α-syn aggregation and neuronal toxicity in parkinsonian models. Mechanistically, EXO-RPM treatment activated both macroautophagy and chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA)-related pathways, thereby promoting autophagic degradation of pathological α-syn. papers.title: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio predicts infusion-site skin nodules in Parkinson's disease patients receiving foslevodopa/foscarbidopa subcutaneous infusion.
papers.abstract: Continuous subcutaneous foslevodopa/foscarbidopa infusion (LDp/CDp-CSI) is an effective treatment for patients with Parkinson's disease (PD), but infusion-site nodules are a major cause of treatment discontinuation. Systemic inflammation can influence local skin tolerance; however, predictive biomarkers remain unidentified. To evaluate the predictive value of the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) for clinically significant infusion-site nodules (PD-CSN) during LDp/CDp-CSI and to establish a clinical management framework to mitigate their development. We prospectively followed 38 patients with PD initiating LDp/CDp-CSI for ≥ 3 months. Baseline immunological data were collected before infusion. A subset of 30 patients was followed for an average of 11 months to identify factors associated with skin nodules at longer follow-up. Nodules were classified by blinded raters. Between-group comparisons, ANCOVA, ROC curve, and Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed. At 3 months, 42% of patients were PD-CSN and showed higher baseline neutrophil counts (P = 0.030) and NLR (P = 0.007), with NLR remaining independently associated with nodule status (F = 7.06, P = 0.012). ROC analysis demonstrated acceptable discrimination (AUC = 0.73, P = 0.016). At last follow-up, lower baseline lymphocyte counts (P = 0.002) and higher NLR (P = 0.001) were observed in PD-CSN. High baseline NLR predicted earlier nodule onset (P = 0.001). Despite frequent nodules, multidisciplinary team surveillance, including remote and in-person follow-up, limited treatment discontinuation to 5.3%. Baseline systemic inflammation, reflected by NLR, predicts both the onset and persistence of infusion-site nodules during LDp/CDp-CSI. NLR may serve as a clinically accessible biomarker for early risk stratification. Multidisciplinary surveillance facilitates timely nodule managem

papers.title: Coupled beta and high-frequency oscillations emerge from synchronized bursting in a minimal model of the parkinsonian subthalamic nucleus.
papers.abstract: Local field potentials (LFPs) recorded from the subthalamic nucleus (STN) in Parkinson's disease (PD) exhibit a distinctive multiscale spectral signature: exaggerated beta-band oscillations (13-30 Hz) coupled to high-frequency oscillations (HFOs, 200-400 Hz), with HFO amplitude being phase-locked to the beta cycle. This phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) has been identified as a promising biomarker of the parkinsonian state, yet no biophysical model has explained how it emerges, what determines the HFO frequency, or how HFOs can exist without beta modulation in the medicated STN. Here we show that a heterogeneous population of excitatory Izhikevich neurons with recurrent coupling produces three dynamical regimes: (i) asynchronous tonic firing, (ii) asynchronous bursting, in which neurons burst individually producing broadband HFO power but without coherent population-level PAC, and (iii) synchronous bursting, which gives rise to beta-HFO PAC. The regimes are governed by two biophysically interpretable parameters that capture complementary effects of dopamine depletion: one reflecting changes in intrinsic neuronal excitability, the other reflecting changes in synaptic coupling strength. The transition from asynchronous to synchronous bursting in this model emulates the emergence of pathological STN neuronal activity in the parkinsonian state. HFO peak frequency varies continuously across the two-parameter landscape, suggesting a possible mechanism of the clinically observed shift from slow (200-300 Hz) to fast (300-400 Hz) HFOs between medication states. The character of the synchronization transition depends on baseline excitability, ranging from a sharp co-emergence of bursting and synchrony at low excitability to a decoupled transition at intermediate excitability, where the bursting fraction saturates while the population synchronization continues to increase with coupling. Superiority of dual-target STN-SNr deep brain stimulation towards gait in Parkinson's disease: a meta-analysis and meta-regression of randomised trials.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effectiveness of a dual-target deep brain stimulation (DBS) approach, stimulating both the subthalamic nucleus (STN) and the substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr), and improvement of gait function and quality of life (QoL) in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD). DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis of crossover randomised controlled trials (RCTs). SETTING: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, ScienceDirect and Scopus databases up to October 2025. PARTICIPANTS: Adults with advanced PD (disease duration >5 years) experiencing clinically significant and refractory freezing of gait (FoG) despite optimal dopaminergic therapy and standard STN-DBS. INTERVENTIONS: Dual-target DBS stimulation of the STN and SNr compared with conventional STN-only stimulation. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: FoG and QoL. RESULTS: Eight crossover RCTs (n=97) were included. Combined STN+SNr resulted in a significant reduction in FoG compared with STN stimulation alone (standard mean difference=-0.39 (95% CI -0.73 to -0.04), I2 CONCLUSIONS: Combined STN and SNr stimulation provides significant clinical benefit for refractory FoG in advanced PD. However, this motor improvement did not translate into immediate QoL gains. Further investigation of RCTs and integrated rehabilitative management are essential to establish broader applicability and its long-term value. PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD42025632066.

papers.title: Animal fluency networks and item-based trajectories in people with Parkinson's disease before and after deep brain stimulation surgery.
papers.abstract: Consistent decline in animal fluency occurs in people with Parkinson's disease (PD) post-surgery for Deep Brain Stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus (STN-DBS). Recent findings indicate that patients produce fewer words after (vs. before) surgery. Also, they produce smaller clusters of related animals, fewer switches between clusters, and more frequent (lexical frequency) and earlier-acquired words. In this paper, we further investigated difficulties in lexical retrieval by reporting on word networks (to study the structure of the mental lexicon) and item-based trajectories (to understand how the linguistic characteristics of the task change as the task progresses) of 61 Dutch-speaking individuals diagnosed with PD before and post-surgery for STN-DBS and 40 age and education-matched healthy controls. Word networks contained a higher number of edges and nodes for healthy controls relative to people with PD post-surgery (adjusting for differences in sample size). Also, patients before surgery produced a network with a lower cluster coefficient relative to healthy controls, as well as to people with PD post-surgery. Item-based trajectories showed that both healthy controls and people with PD produced words of increasing complexity as they proceed with the task (e.g., less frequent, acquired later, of higher length). Also, healthy controls showed a steeper increase in the age of acquisition of words across the first ten responses compared to PD post-surgery. The re-emergence of structure (clustering) in word networks post-surgery for STN-DBS and the differences in item-based trajectories (vs. healthy controls) represent novel markers of lexical retrieval that are affected by surgery for STN-DBS and PD.

papers.title: Accuracy and clinical outcomes of robot-assisted deep brain stimulation lead placement using a floor-mounted robotic navigation system: a prospective multicenter study.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate clinical data to assess the accuracy and safety of a new robot system used for deep brain stimulation (DBS) lead placement. METHODS: A prospective, multicenter, single-arm study included 60 patients indicated for DBS. Patients aged 18-85 years with Parkinson's disease, essential tremor, or dystonia were enrolled. The primary outcome was electrode accuracy at the tip, 40 mm from the tip, and the entry point compared with the planned trajectory. Secondary outcomes included operative time (OT), length of stay (LOS), and perioperative complications through discharge. RESULTS: The cohort (mean age 67.1 ± 9.9 years) primarily consisted of patients with Parkinson's disease (n = 46). The mean OT was 159.0 ± 26.7 minutes, and the mean LOS was 1.6 ± 1.5 days. The complication rate and return to the operating room rate were both 0%. The mean tip error was 0.8 ± 0.5 mm, error at 40 mm from the tip was 0.4 ± 0.5 mm, and entry point error was 1.0 ± 0.8 mm. CONCLUSIONS: DBS electrode implantation using the new robot-assisted system demonstrated high plan-to-place accuracy comparable or superior to historical frame-based and robotic platforms. The safety profile and operative efficiency, reflected by very low complication rates and similar OT and LOS to published literature, support the system as a viable alternative to standard frame-based stereotaxy.

papers.title: Caregivers' Knowledge and Timing of Palliative Care in Parkinson's Disease: A Survey Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Palliative care is underused in Parkinson's disease (PD) and often initiated only in the final days of life. Caregivers shape health care decisions as cognitive impairment advances, yet how PD caregivers specifically compare in perceived versus actual knowledge and what they believe about the timing of initiation remain incompletely characterized. OBJECTIVES: The aim of the study was to compare perceived and actual palliative care knowledge among PD caregivers, characterize beliefs about optimal timing of initiation, and identify associated factors. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey of informal caregivers was conducted at the Movement Disorders Clinic, Baycrest Health Sciences Centre, Toronto. Caregivers with health care training were excluded. Perceived knowledge was rated on a six-point scale; actual knowledge was assessed with true/false items benchmarked against the World Health Organization (WHO) palliative care definition. Sex differences were tested with Wilcoxon rank-sum and Fisher's exact tests (P < 0.05). RESULTS: Fifty-two caregivers participated (mean age 54 years; 50% female; 84.6% adult children). Ninety-two percent rated their knowledge as good or excellent, yet 88.5% endorsed the belief that palliative care is primarily for dying patients, the only item a majority answered incorrectly. Accuracy on remaining items ranged from 75% to 100%. Among caregivers whose relative had received palliative care, 73.1% recalled initiation at Hoehn and Yahr stage 5, although 50% preferred earlier initiation. Agreement with early integration exceeded 82% across all 20 attitude items. No sex differences observed. CONCLUSIONS: PD caregivers combine high self-rated knowledge with a singular misconception equating palliative care with dying, alongside a preference for earlier integration. The pattern indicates a system-level referral gap rather than caregiver resistance and supports clinic-embedded education and proactive, stage-decoupled

papers.title: Wearable Evidence Linking Dyskinesia Burden to Sleep Quality in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sleep disturbances affect 60-80% of people with Parkinson's disease (PD) and worsen quality of life. Dyskinesia is a common complication of dopaminergic therapy, yet its link to sleep quality is poorly understood. OBJECTIVES: To examine whether clinician-rated and objectively measured dyskinesia are associated with sleep quality in PD. METHODS: We studied 47 people with PD (median age 68 years; 44.7% women; median disease duration 5 years). Sleep was measured with Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Dyskinesia was rated clinically (MDS-UPDRS items 4.1, 4.2) and objectively over 7 days using Parkinson's KinetiGraph (median dyskinesia score; DKS). Regression models adjusted for age, sex, motor severity, levodopa dose, and disease duration. RESULTS: All dyskinesia measures predicted poorer sleep unadjusted. After adjusting for levodopa dose, only DKS remained significant (B = 0.18, P = 0.047). Adding disease duration attenuated this (P = 0.051). CONCLUSIONS: Wearable-derived dyskinesia, but not clinician-rated dyskinesia, independently predicted poorer sleep, supporting wearable monitoring in PD.

papers.title: Exome Sequencing Identifies Population-Specific Genetic Risk Factors for Progressive Supranuclear Palsy in Asia.
papers.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a debilitating primary tauopathy. Although genome-wide association studies have identified risk loci in European populations, the genetic architecture of PSP in Asia remains largely undefined. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to identify population-specific genetic risk factors in Asian patients with PSP. METHODS: We performed whole-exome sequencing in 549 patients with PSP recruited across East and Southeast Asia. Variant frequencies were compared with 1492 whole-genome-sequenced controls from the Taiwan Biobank. Novel variants were functionally evaluated using cellular and Drosophila models. RESULTS: Among 549 patients (mean age at onset 65.1 ± 7.4 years; 60.47% male), 29 (5.28%) carried heterozygous pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, including 12 novel variants. Additionally, 127 patients (23.13%) harbored 144 rare variants of uncertain significance with minor allele frequency < 1%. Pathogenic variants were most frequently identified in ABCA7 (n = 6, 20.69%) and SMPD1 (n = 6, 20.69%), followed by BSN (n = 3, 10.34%) and MAPT (n = 2, 6.90%). Rare variant landscape analysis identified BSN as the most prominent contributor (38/173 total rare variants, 21.97%), followed by ABCA7 (13.29%), LRRK2 (10.40%), and MAPT (6.94%). Functional studies demonstrated that BSN variants enhance tau aggregation and neurodegeneration. Additionally, the common Asian LRRK2 variants were enriched in PSP, with p.G2385R significantly associated with PSP risk (odds ratio 2.75, 95% CI 1.77-4.32; P < 0.0001) and remained significant compared with Taiwan Biobank controls (P = 0.02), whereas the association for p.R1628P was attenuated. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings delineate an ancestry-specific genetic architecture of PSP distinct from the MAPT-dominant pattern observed in European populations, providing mechanistic insights into
